_purpose: Canonical 3D-scene vantages for the visual-regression + perf sweeps (scripts/probe-sweep.js). This is the golden spec: each vantage teleports the probe to a fixed camera + time/sea, captures one screenshot, and records fps. The `expect` text is what a correct frame looks like; `regressions` lists the specific failures this vantage exists to catch (each has bitten a real release). Data-driven per the infinite-of-x rule - add a vantage here, both sweeps pick it up. Coordinates are the same debug/camera_request.json + debug/showcase_request.json fields lib.rs polls.
_perf_note: perf_floor_fps is an advisory lower bound at this vantage on the dev machine (RTX 4070). The perf sweep flags a stop below it; it is a smoke threshold, not a hard gate.
_clock_note: READ THIS BEFORE PICKING A `time`. The showcase `time` field is a GLOBAL clock, not the local solar hour at the vantage (src/engine/ipc.rs:200-205 feeds it straight into the world clock). The local solar hour is roughly `time + lon/15`. So time 12.0 is local noon only near lon 0; at lon 138.8 (the Fuji vantages) time 12.0 is about 21:15 LOCAL and the frame comes back as a night scene. Pick `time = desired_local_hour - lon/15`, wrapped into 0..24. This trap cost `ground-storm-inslab` its whole purpose from v0.1070 to v0.1073: it was installed as the permanent BUG-049 daylight gate and was silently rendering at night, so every cloud LIGHTING change was being judged in the dark.

vantages.desc: Ground level near Mt Fuji in a conifer forest, morning
vantages._settle_note: 75 s, NOT the 25 s this carried through v0.1078. MEASURED 2026-07-31: at 25 s this vantage captures 43-48 ms while the scene is still streaming, and it keeps getting heavier for another ~40 s before it settles at 93.7 ms +/- 5.8 (10.7 fps) on the operator's max-quality rig config. So the sweep was reporting 21.3 and 18.8 fps and passing an 18 fps floor at 55% of the real number. Every perf figure taken here before v0.1079 is measuring a half-built forest. probe-sweep.js `settle_s` is a plain sleep (scripts/probe-sweep.js:236) with no steady-state detection; a proper fix waits for [PatchBatch] to stop changing in run.log, which is a rig change, not a data change.
vantages._hold_altitude_note: Added v0.1081. Without it the walking player comes to rest on different ground every run - [NearTree] recompute reported alt 1240 / 1364 / 1376 / 1424 m across four runs of a byte-identical config, frame time swung 39.7 to 85.3 ms (2.15x), and 2 of those 4 runs failed to capture at all ("screenshot: null" / "camera: null"). camera_request parks the player but leaves gravity acting during the 75 s settle; the re-park at scripts/probe-sweep.js:254 pins the pose once the patches are built. fuji-forest-hillside already carried this key.
vantages.expect: Dense green ground with real 3D conifer trees standing around the camera - visible brown trunks, needled canopies - and BAKED SILHOUETTE cards, ragged crown outlines with sky visible through their edges, never plain rectangles, carrying the forest toward the horizon. Grass underfoot. BACKLIT FOLIAGE GLOWS: crowns seen against the sky read as luminous yellow-green with visible leaf structure, never as black shards.
regressions: 3D tree MODELS present, not just flat cards (v0.923 default-off regression)
no bare ground where a forest should be (bare-forest card-hide bug)
trunks visible, not floating canopies

NO flat rectangular slabs anywhere in the tree field: every card past the 3D-model ring shows a crown outline with sky visible through its edge. 6 of the 8 rows in data/vegetation/trees.ron are procedural (model: "") and had NO atlas tile, so they fell through planet_chunks.rs:1925 to plain coloured trunk+canopy rectangles; fir and pine took the sprite path but a SHIPPED build has no assets/models/ (.github/workflows/build-desktop.yml copies data/ + assets/icons/ + assets/shaders/ only), so the bake aborted, tree_atlas_ready stayed false and their cards painted the flat green fallback at 90-fragment-main.wgsl:824. Photographed as a picket fence of grey slabs at v0.1078.

NO storm-strength lean in calm weather: the same wind uniform (light7_cone_inner, wind_dir_world.xyz + speed m/s) must produce a near-upright stand here. Crowns sway but stay centred over their bases.

NO black backlit canopy. In the crop (900,0)-(1700,500) the MEDIAN luminance of canopy pixels must be at least 0.10x the median of sky pixels in the same crop, and fewer than 30% of canopy pixels may fall below luma 16. MEASUREMENT: luma = 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B; a pixel is SKY if B > R and B > G (the dome is blue-dominant, foliage never is) and CANOPY otherwise - note that lumps trunks, branches and deep interior gaps in with the leaves, which is why the dark-fraction half of the gate is 30% and not 20%. MEASURED v0.1080.1 (before): ratio 0.026, dark fraction 58.5% (the finding's own slightly different classifier read 0.063 / 53.9% on its capture). MEASURED v0.1081 (after): ratio 0.448, dark fraction 22.8%, same rig, same config, same crop. Cause of the failure: tree_mesh::blade() emitted through PlantMeshBuilder::tri2, which never sets self.organ, so every foliage face on sakura/momiji/oak/birch/acacia (and every blossom) carried Organ::Stem, bit 19 was clear, 90-fragment-main.wgsl:1157 is_leaf was false, and the canopy was shaded by the BARK branch at :1259 with no transmission at all. Palm was the only correct species. The leaf-flutter gate at 00-bindings-vertex.wgsl:682 reads the same bit, so v0.1080 foliage wind had no flutter on any procedural tree either. MEASURED AT 2560x1387, AND THIS GATE IS RESOLUTION DEPENDENT: the residual dark is geometric aliasing of sub-pixel leaf blades (no MSAA - every MultisampleState in src/renderer/pipeline.rs is count 1), so the SAME v0.1081 build measures 0.448 / 22.8% at 2560x1387 and 0.211 / 35.3% at 1280x720. The ratio half passes at both widths; the dark-fraction half passes at 2560 and FAILS at 1280. Judge this only on a 2560-wide capture and record the capture width in the manifest - a second rig running concurrently can silently change the window size, which is exactly how the 1280x720 reading was produced.

CARD/MODEL SIZE MATCH at the handoff: capture the same acacia or palm from just inside and just outside tree_model_distance (120 m). The silhouette height must agree within 10% and the trunk base must sit on the ground in both, with NO vertical hop as the camera crosses the ring. Cards are emitted h x h (planet_chunks.rs:1717 `let w = h;`) while the baker frames a square on max(width, height) and returns a footprint the atlas builder discards as _fp (billboard_bake.rs:167-171 and :103), so a crown WIDER than the tree is tall renders about 27% too short with its trunk base about 13% of the card height off the ground. Acacia is that case by construction (tree_mesh.rs:545, "the crown is WIDER than the tree is tall"); fir and pine are height-dominant, which is why the defect was invisible while only they took the sprite path. This is a MOTION gate - walk the ring, do not just compare two stills.

FIR AND PINE MUST BE VISIBLE IN A SHIPPED BUILD. They are invisible today (audited at v0.1085, from source, all three legs confirmed) at EVERY distance, and THIS RIG CANNOT SEE IT. (1) The near-model builder generates a procedural mesh only for rows where is_procedural() (src/lib.rs:9382); fir/pine carry model: "fir_sapling" / "pine_sapling_small" so they get none, their glTF is absent from a release bundle (.github/workflows/build-desktop.yml copies data/ + assets/icons/ + assets/shaders/ ONLY - assets/models/ and assets/textures/ never ship), and the draw loop `continue`s on the cache miss (src/lib.rs:9646). (2) The card baker skips them the same way, logs "[Bake] fir v0: no model parts (assets/models/ absent?), tile N left empty" and leaves the atlas tile transparent (src/renderer/billboard_bake.rs:297-306). (3) The sprite branch then discards every texel of that empty tile at `spr.a < 0.5` (assets/shaders/pbr/90-fragment-main.wgsl:833). Nothing errors, because tree_atlas_ready stays true on the 6 procedural species that do bake. CONSEQUENCE, from the elevation gates in data/vegetation/trees.ron: at this vantage (lat 35.3, ~1245 m) fir+pine are 2.0 of the 8.2 passing weight, so ~24% of the stand is missing; above 1600 m at this latitude and above 2000 m anywhere on Earth, fir and pine are the ONLY species whose gates pass, so a shipped build shows a COMPLETELY BARE alpine forest up to the 3000/3200 m treeline. The rig junctions the whole repo assets/ into the sandbox (scripts/probe-sweep.js:90), so every sweep runs with 62 photoscans present that no player has. Judge this only in a --shipped-assets rig that junctions assets/icons and assets/shaders alone. FIX: build a procedural form mesh for every registry row - tree_mesh::build_tree already dispatches purely on def.form (src/renderer/tree_mesh.rs:441-447) and fir/pine already carry form: "conifer" - and fall back to proc:{id}_v{va} when the glTF key is absent.
vantages._fidelity_note: 2026-08-01 (v0.1085 vegetation domain pass): this vantage was measured in detail - canopy/sky median-luma ratio 0.237, 36.7% of solid canopy pixels both dark (luma<30) and achromatic (chroma<12), crown top-third/bottom-third luma 1.30 / 0.92 / 0.65 / 0.67 across four boxes, forest-floor 8x8 tile-mean SD 1.3 (2-4 m) and 1.9 (3-8 m), plus leaf-normal statistics from a bit-exact replica of the generator RNG (74.4-78.3% of camera-facing blade faces are undersides against 61.2% for a spherical leaf-angle distribution). DO NOT paste any of those numbers into the gates above. Two independent reasons: the capture was 1280x720 while the gates here are specified at 2560 wide and the backlit-canopy gate is provably resolution dependent (0.448/22.8% at 2560 vs 0.211/35.3% at 1280 on the SAME build), and the frame contained 62 photoscan fir/pine that a shipped build does not have (see the FIR AND PINE regression above). Re-baseline at 2560 in a --shipped-assets rig before any of it becomes a gate.
vantages._perf_floor_note: Restated 18 -> 9 at v0.1081. The 18 was written against 25 s captures of a half-streamed forest; this vantage's own _settle_note records the settled truth as 93.7 ms +/- 5.8 = 10.7 fps, and fresh v0.1080.1 captures returned 10 fps. The floor was already violated before anyone touched foliage, so at 18 the next writer to add a shader term gets blamed for a pre-existing miss. 9 fps is a real floor under the measured settled state. Do NOT use this vantage for A/B frame-time work even now that hold_altitude pins the pose - use ground-storm-inslab (50.7 +/- 1.8 ms, n=3), which is the reproducible perf vantage. CAVEAT ADDED v0.1081.1, READ BEFORE TRUSTING ANY NUMBER IN THIS NOTE: src/lib.rs:2882 clamps the frame delta with .min(0.1) and the SAME clamped dt stamps the perf counters at :11551 and :11555, which src/engine/ipc.rs:549-550 writes into screenshot_done.json and scripts/probe-sweep.js:269-270 records. fps therefore saturates at exactly 10.0 and frame_ms at exactly 100.0, so a 9 fps floor CANNOT FAIL and every figure above (93.7 ms, 10.7 fps, 50.7 ms) is a censored sample biased toward 100 ms. Timed off the log instead, between consecutive 60-frame [ChunkDiag] lines (src/lib.rs:8909), this forest runs about 131 ms / 7.6 fps where the rig reported 99.1. Unclamp the counters (keep the clamp for the simulation dt, stamp fps and the ring from a raw_dt, and report the ring's MEDIAN alongside its mean), then re-measure and restate this whole note. See docs/design/vegetation-cards-every-species.md precondition P2.

vantages._camera_note: altitude_km 0.15 -> 0.6 and look_offset_deg 72 -> 55 (v0.1082, after a 1.0/52 detour). The vantage AS FIRST WRITTEN NEVER GOT ABOVE THE CANOPY: at altitude_km 0.15 it captured "Alt: 0 m" and framed identically to fuji-forest-ground, so all three of its above-canopy gates were unevaluable and read as passing only because nothing evaluated them. poll_camera_request (src/engine/ipc.rs) parks above a SAMPLED ground radius which under-reads the DRAWN Fuji surface by about 320 m. Transfer function measured at this lat/lon: requested 0.15 -> Alt 0 m, 0.30 -> 0, 0.60 -> 353, 1.20 -> 880. Over water the same path is exact (ocean-700m captures Alt 713 m), so this is land-only. WHY 0.6 AND NOT 1.0: the runtime verifier flew the 1.0/52 aim (834 m eye) and its one clear frame showed a BARE slope with zero trees, because at that altitude the lower-two-thirds band sits BEYOND the 1500 m card cutoff (independently confirming the NO-VEGETATION-RING defect). 0.6/55 is the MEASURED pose that produced the crown-structure baselines with canopy visibly in frame at a 353 m eye - use the pose that was measured to work, not an interpolated one.
vantages.expect: A forested slope filling the lower two-thirds of the frame, seen from well above the canopy: individual crowns readable as separate ragged silhouettes with a clear sunlit-top / shaded-flank split, the canopy mass reading DARKER than the open ground beyond it. (Forest-to-the-horizon is NOT expected yet: the 1500 m card cutoff hard-ends the vegetation - that is the NO-VEGETATION-RING gate's defect, fixed by the Bayer fade, and only after that fix should this expect be upgraded. look_offset_deg is measured from straight down, so 55 aims about 35 degrees below the horizon. showcase `time` is a GLOBAL clock; local solar hour = time + lon/15, so lon 138.8 needs time 2.9 for local noon - see _clock_note.)
regressions: THE VANTAGE MUST ACTUALLY BE ABOVE THE CANOPY: the HUD Alt readout must exceed 250 m (trees are ~20 m; 353 m measured at this pose) and no trunk base may appear at eye level. MEASURED 2026-07-31 at v0.1081: requested altitude_km 0.15 captured Alt 0 m and framed identically to fuji-forest-ground, because the camera parks above a SAMPLED ground radius that under-reads the drawn Fuji surface by about 320 m (0.15 -> 0, 0.3 -> 0, 0.6 -> 353, 1.2 -> 880 m measured at this lat/lon; over water the same path is exact, ocean-700m captures 713 m). Every above-canopy gate below was unevaluable until the altitude was raised. If a future rig change makes altitude exact, this gate still holds; if a capture comes back at eye level, do not judge anything else in this list from it.
NO flat rectangular slabs in the canopy band - the finding-1 gate, at the distance where it is most visible

the forest band's mean luminance must be BELOW that of the adjacent open ground (real canopy albedo 0.08-0.15 vs grass 0.20-0.25). Card shading normals were pinned to the radial up at planet_chunks.rs:1686 and :1727 (the v0.896 black-slab fix), so cards lit exactly like the terrain and a distant forest read as a flat green carpet painted on the hillside. MEASURED at v0.1081 from an 880 m eye: the forest disc read 29.9 against open slope 79.2, so the albedo half of this was already right - it is the crown-scale STRUCTURE gate below that fails.

CROWN-SCALE STRUCTURE (the "flat carpet" gate, given a number at v0.1081.1; threshold restated v0.1082 at the conditions it was MEASURED at): in the canopy band the stddev of 16x16 px TILE MEANS must be at least 15/255 on a 1280x720 capture in box (350,300)-(950,500) - scale the box and tile size proportionally at other widths, and re-baseline before judging at 2560 - and per-tree luminance variance in the band must exceed 8/255. MEASUREMENT: luma = 0.2126R + 0.7152G + 0.0722B; tile the canopy box into 16x16 px blocks, take each block's mean, take the stddev of those means. MEASURED 2026-07-31 at v0.1081 (1280x720, box 350,300-950,500, 353 m eye): 4.93 for the card band against 47.29 for the 3D-model band in the same session, a 9.6x deficit at crown scale - the card canopy holds one tenth the crown-scale contrast of the real canopy it hands off from. Multi-scale for reference, card band vs model band at 1/2/4/8/16/32 px: 14.97/11.28/8.81/6.65/4.93/4.16 against 72.55/64.23/58.80/53.78/47.29/39.66; all of the card band's variance is pixel-scale noise.

NO VEGETATION RING at the card cutoff: across the cutoff radius on a single continuous slope, the mean luminance step must be under 15% and the local (8x8 px) SD ratio under 2.0. MEASURED 2026-07-31 at v0.1081 from an 880 m eye: inside 29.9 mean luma / local SD 8.13, outside 45.5 / 1.18 - a 34% step and a 6.9x texture step, with the boundary tracking the camera. The card stage hard-discards with no fade at 90-fragment-main.wgsl:805 (sprite branch) and :842 (coloured branch) on tree_card_far_m, 1500 m; the fix is the 4x4 Bayer dissolve already used for grass at :853-866, over the last ~250 m of the card range.

NO black slabs either: the v0.896 failure this replaced. A card normal blended toward the card facing must never reach N.L = 0 under an overhead sun, and a two-sided card must not go dark on its back face
